Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- A former hospital worker systematically shot and killed four people in upstate New York on Saturday, authorities in two counties said. Former hospital worker Frank Garcia, 34, has been accused in the shooting rampage. Frank Garcia, 34, was arrested Saturday afternoon. Garcia knew all four victims, police said, but they didn't reveal details about the relationships. "The individuals who were shot were known to the suspect. It was not necessarily a random act," Monroe County Sheriff Patrick O'Flynn said. The first two victims -- Mary Sillman, 23, and Randall Norman, 41 -- were fatally shot before 5 a.m. at Lakeside Memorial Hospital in Brockport, where Garcia was once employed, O'Flynn said. Another woman was wounded and is undergoing treatment at a nearby hospital, he said. The second shooting happened at a house in nearby Ontario County on Saturday afternoon. Christopher Glatz, 45, and his wife, Kim, 38, were killed "execution-style" while their two teenagers were in the suburban Rochester home, Ontario County Sheriff Philip Povero said. The teens were not wounded, but it is unclear whether they witnessed the event. Povero said neighbors reported Garcia went door-to-door looking for the Glatzes' home. "He was in fact looking for the residence," Povero said. "He was saying different things to different people, but he was clearly looking for that home." Ballistic evidence has connected the two crime scenes, Povero said. Investigators found the matching brass cartridges from a pistol found on Garcia when he was arrested, he said. Garcia was arrested at a restaurant Saturday afternoon, CNN affiliate R-News in Rochester reported. Garcia was to be arraigned Saturday night in Monroe County, where the first shootings occurred, on two counts of first-degree murder and one count of attempted murder in the second degree, O'Flynn said. Sillman was a certified nursing assistant at Lakeside's long-term care center, hospital officials said. "During Mary's brief time within the system, those who worked closest with Mary described her as warm, kind and compassionate toward the residents of Lakeside Beikirch Care Center," Lakeside interim CEO Michael Stapleton said in a statement. Garcia likely will face similar charges in Ontario County, Povero said. "This certainly speaks to a tragedy that is enormous, not only the taking of the lives that were taken, but the people that were left behind, the person in Brockport and the two teenage children who were present when their mother was systematically murdered," Povero said.

# Former Hospital Employee Charged in Deadly Four-Victim Shooting Spree Across Upstate New York

(CNN) — Authorities in two New York counties reported that a former hospital worker orchestrated a methodical shooting spree on Saturday, claiming the lives of four individuals. Frank Garcia, 34, has been charged in connection with the killings and was taken into custody Saturday afternoon.

According to police, Garcia was acquainted with all four victims, though authorities declined to elaborate on the nature of these relationships. "The individuals who were shot were known to the suspect. It was not necessarily a random act," explained Monroe County Sheriff Patrick O'Flynn.

The violence began before 5 a.m., when two victims—Mary Sillman, 23, and Randall Norman, 41—were fatally shot at Lakeside Memorial Hospital in Brockport, an institution where Garcia had previously worked, O'Flynn stated. A third woman sustained injuries in the attack and remains under treatment at a nearby medical facility.

The rampage continued that afternoon at a residence in neighboring Ontario County, where Christopher Glatz, 45, and his wife Kim, 38, were killed in what authorities described as an "execution-style" attack. The couple's two teenage children were present in their suburban Rochester home at the time, though they escaped physical harm, according to Ontario County Sheriff Philip Povero. It remains uncertain whether the teenagers witnessed the attack.

Povero noted that neighbors had observed Garcia canvassing the area, apparently searching for the Glatz residence. "He was in fact looking for the residence," Povero said. "He was saying different things to different people, but he was clearly looking for that home."

Investigators established a forensic link between the two crime scenes through ballistic evidence, Povero confirmed, noting that matching brass cartridges were traced to a pistol recovered from Garcia at the time of his arrest.

According to CNN affiliate R-News in Rochester, Garcia was apprehended at a local restaurant Saturday afternoon. He was scheduled to be arraigned that evening in Monroe County—the site of the initial shootings—facing two counts of first-degree murder and one count of second-degree attempted murder, O'Flynn said.

Hospital officials confirmed that Sillman had worked as a certified nursing assistant at Lakeside's long-term care facility. "During Mary's brief time within the system, those who worked closest with Mary described her as warm, kind and compassionate toward the residents of Lakeside Beikirch Care Center," said Michael Stapleton, Lakeside's interim CEO, in a released statement.

Frank Garcia, a 34-year-old former hospital employee, was taken into custody Saturday afternoon in connection with a deadly shooting spree that left four people dead across two New York counties. Authorities have confirmed that Garcia was acquainted with all four victims, emphasizing that the killings were not the result of random violence. The violence began before 5 a.m. at Lakeside Memorial Hospital in Brockport, an institution where Garcia had previously been employed. During this initial attack, two hospital employees—Mary Sillman and Randall Norman—were shot and killed. A third woman was wounded in the incident but survived her injuries. Hours later, in the afternoon, the violence continued at a residence in Ontario County belonging to Christopher and Kim Glatz. According to authorities, the couple was killed in what has been described as an "execution-style" manner, suggesting a deliberate and calculated approach to the killings. # Former Hospital Employee Kills Three in Workplace Shooting, Police Say

**By CNN Staff**

*(CNN)* — A former hospital employee opened fire at a medical facility in suburban Ohio on Tuesday morning, killing three people before being taken into custody by police, according to law enforcement officials.

The shooting occurred at approximately 8:15 a.m. at Meridian Regional Medical Center in Fairview Heights, a suburb located roughly 20 miles outside Columbus. Authorities identified the suspect as 47-year-old Gregory Hansen, who was terminated from his position as a hospital maintenance supervisor approximately eight months ago.

"This individual specifically targeted former colleagues," said Fairview Heights Police Chief Maria Delgado at a press conference Tuesday afternoon. "Based on our preliminary investigation, this does not appear to be a random act of violence."

## Victims Identified

Police identified the victims as 52-year-old Patricia Nolan, a hospital administrator; 38-year-old James Okafor, a facilities manager; and 61-year-old Ruth Bellweather, a longtime billing department employee. All three had worked directly with Hansen prior to his termination.

Hospital officials confirmed that Hansen's employment was terminated following what they described as "a series of workplace conduct violations," though they declined to elaborate further, citing the ongoing investigation.

## Timeline of Events

According to witnesses, Hansen entered through a service entrance he was previously authorized to use, suggesting he may have retained access credentials or exploited a security gap. He proceeded to the administrative wing, where he allegedly confronted Nolan in her office before the shooting began.

"We heard what sounded like arguing, and then the shots," said Maria Chen, a nurse who was in a nearby hallway. "People were running everywhere. It was chaos."

The hospital was placed on lockdown within minutes, and SWAT teams responded to the scene. Hansen was apprehended in the parking garage approximately 40 minutes after the first 911 call, police said. He did not resist arrest.

## Suspect's Background

Neighbors described Hansen as a quiet man who had become increasingly isolated since losing his job. "He kept to himself mostly, but lately he seemed angry — you could just tell something was off," said neighbor Robert Timmons.

Court records show Hansen had no prior criminal history. However, sources close to the investigation say he had made concerning statements to acquaintances in recent weeks, though it remains unclear whether these were reported to authorities.

## Investigation Continues

The FBI is assisting local police in the investigation. Authorities are working to determine how Hansen obtained the firearm used in the attack and whether he had specifically planned the killings in advance.

Hansen has been charged with three counts of murder and is being held without bail. He is scheduled to appear in court Thursday.

Meridian Regional Medical Center released a statement expressing condolences to the victims' families and announced it would be enhancing security protocols, including revoking building access immediately upon employee termination.

Grief counselors have been made available to hospital staff, and the facility resumed limited operations Wednesday morning.

*This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.*

---

*CNN's Sarah Mitchell and David Park contributed to this report.*
